---
title: "BGC Roster"
subtitle: "The sortable table of matching iBGCs"
---

The **BGC roster** is the default view of your results: one row per integrated BGC ([iBGC](key-concepts.qmd#ibgc-integrated-bgc)) matching the current query. It is the fastest way to rank candidates and to read their key attributes side by side.

The roster is empty until you press **Run Query** (or have an active filter, search, or loaded asset).

![The BGC roster, sorted by novelty. Each row is one iBGC; badges flag validated and partial clusters (type-strain and submitted clusters are flagged the same way).](images/roster.png)

## Columns

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **iBGC** | The iBGC accession/label. Badges flag **Validated**, **Type Strain**, **Submitted** (your uploaded asset), and **Partial** (runs off the contig edge). |
| **Sim.** | Similarity to your query — only meaningful after a search. Its label changes with the search type (see below). |
| **Class** | The normalised [BGC class](bgc-classes.qmd) (Polyketide, NRPS, RiPP, …). |
| **Size (kb)** | Length of the cluster in kilobases. |
| **Novelty** | Distance from the nearest validated cluster (0–1; higher = more novel). |
| **Dom. nov.** | Domain novelty — fraction of domains unique within the iBGC's GCF. |
| **Sources** | The detection tools that called this cluster (antiSMASH, GECCO, SanntiS, …). |
| **Assembly** | The parent assembly accession. |
| **Collection** | The source collection the assembly came from. |

Scores shown as "—" could not be computed for that iBGC (see [Scores & Metrics](scores-metrics.qmd)).

## Sorting

Click a sortable column header to sort; click again to reverse. Sortable columns are **Size**, **Novelty**, **Dom. nov.**, and **Sim.** The default sort is **Novelty**, descending — so the most novel candidates appear first.

After a [sequence search](sequence-search.qmd) or a [Find similar iBGCs](similar-ibgc.qmd) run, the roster automatically sorts by the query similarity so the table mirrors the search ranking. You can override this at any time by clicking another header.

## How the similarity column adapts to the search

The second column reflects whichever search produced the results:

- **No search** — there is no meaningful similarity, so it shows "—".
- **Domain or Find-similar search** — it shows a domain-based similarity score (0–1).
- **Sequence search** — it is replaced by two columns: **Bitscore** (the phmmer alignment score of the best-matching protein) and **Best hit** (the protein ID of that match).

## Selecting and acting on rows

- **Left-click** a row to load that iBGC into the [Compare](ibgc-detail.qmd) panel.
- **Right-click** a row for the actions menu: **Set as reference iBGC**, **Find similar iBGCs**, and **Add to shortlist**.

Submitted (uploaded-asset) iBGCs are shaded amber so they stand out against catalogue rows.

## Paging and bulk shortlisting

The footer shows the total match count and pages through results 50 at a time. **Add all to shortlist** adds every iBGC matching the current query — not just the visible page — up to the shortlist cap. If the query matched more than the considered limit, a note tells you how many were matched versus added, so you know the selection was truncated.
